claims.statement: Provider-specific wrappers adapt model-facing SDK methods to `traceable` LLM runs while preserving provider call and streaming interfaces; stream chunks are accumulated through provider reducers into normalized final outputs before the run ends.

The JavaScript Anthropic wrapper transforms only the traced copy of request inputs: it masks transport secrets and MCP credentials and converts `system` content into a leading system message without modifying the request sent to Anthropic.
Anthropic usage normalization treats cache-read and cache-creation tokens as additive input tokens and preserves cache categories in normalized input-token details.

The Vercel AI SDK integration composes orchestration, model, and tool adaptation: `wrapAISDK` wraps generate, stream, object, and optional `ToolLoopAgent` APIs, `LangSmithMiddleware` creates child LLM runs, and tool `execute` functions become tool runs with separately resolved child configuration.

Vercel model streaming passes chunks through unchanged while collecting text, reasoning, tool calls, finish metadata, and usage; on flush it formats the aggregate, ends the child RunTree, and patches it, with raw HTTP details excluded unless explicitly enabled.

The JavaScript OpenAI Agents tracing processor maps trace and span lifecycle callbacks into a RunTree hierarchy, delays posts until meaningful inputs are available, restores AsyncLocalStorage context on end, and forces tracing on for processor-created roots so nested traceable tool calls are captured.

OpenAI Agents integration metadata merges processor and per-trace values, maps the SDK group identifier to `thread_id`, preserves explicit agent-type values, and structurally classifies guardrails as middleware and agents nested beneath tools as subagents.

The OpenAI Realtime integration proxies the original connection, observes iteration and receive events, maintains turn and transcript state, records model output and normalized usage at `response.done`, and owns root/session teardown through an async context manager.

Frameworks that already emit OpenTelemetry spans use a translate-then-forward processor chain: the shared voice processor captures thread context, rewrites a draft at span end, rebuilds a new readable span, and forwards it downstream only after translation; translation failures are isolated and may export the span untranslated.

OpenTelemetry support is optional: JavaScript keeps OTel imports out of its singleton and uses no-op instances until initialized, while Python OTel integrations report an actionable optional-dependency error and Python client OTel modes fall back to LangSmith-only tracing when the packages are unavailable.

Global OpenTelemetry ownership is explicit: Python `configure()` installs a provider only when OTel is still in its proxy/no-op state and otherwise directs callers to add `OtelSpanProcessor` to the existing provider; JavaScript `initializeOTEL()` can install a context manager and a default provider, but when a custom provider is passed it returns the LangSmith processor without attaching it.

The JavaScript native OTLP exporter derives LangSmith endpoint, API-key, and project defaults, honors an explicit URL and standard OTel endpoint/header overrides, and supports a last-mile span transform; Python's public native `OtelExporter` derives a full LangSmith trace endpoint, API-key, project, and custom headers, while `OtelSpanProcessor` batches spans and can stamp OTel-safe LangSmith metadata at span start.

In Python OTel tracing mode, the internal exporter turns serialized RunTree post/update operations into deterministic OTel spans, maps run metadata, I/O, status, model, tools, and usage into LangSmith and GenAI attributes, and maintains a thread-safe in-flight store whose stale orphan spans are periodically ended and removed.

OpenTelemetry span translators rebuild a new `ReadableSpan` with rewritten attributes or events while preserving the original span's other fields, rather than mutating the original read-only span representation.

RunTree ingestion is a create-then-update lifecycle: `postRun()` sends normalized initial run data, while `patchRun()` sends completion fields and normally excludes inputs so a batched update cannot overwrite create-time inputs; callers can explicitly set `excludeInputs: false` to persist inputs added later.

Native OTel processors and RunTree-to-OTel translation have separate queue boundaries: native spans go directly through their OTel processor/exporter chain, whereas translated run creates and updates first traverse the LangSmith SDK client batch queue before the translator and configured OTel provider own span export.

In JavaScript OTel tracing mode, `traceable` starts an active marked OTel span, the client captures its context with queued create/update operations, and `LangSmithToOTELTranslator` enriches and retains the span on post and updates or ends it on patch; a post with no active span in the captured context is skipped.

Python tracing mode resolves to `langsmith`, `otel`, or `hybrid`; OTel modes use a supplied provider, then an initialized global provider, or create a LangSmith OTLP provider, while hybrid queue handling sends the same combined operations independently to LangSmith ingest and the OTel translator so one leg's failure does not stop the other.

The SDK-managed OTLP bootstrap in both Python and JavaScript defaults to `{LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT}/otel/v1/traces`; a full `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` overrides the base `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, while a base endpoint is suffixed with `/v1/traces`, and an ends-in-`/traces` base is temporarily preserved with a legacy compatibility warning.

Flush and shutdown follow queue ownership: JavaScript `awaitPendingTraceBatches()` drains the SDK queue and force-flushes its registered default OTel processor, `LangSmithOTLPSpanProcessor.shutdown()` waits for shared RunTree batches before inherited processor shutdown, Python `Client.flush()` drains its run-operation queue, and Python's public OTel processor separately delegates force-flush and shutdown to its inner processor.
